scenes.heading: Spheres: surface area and volume
scenes.say: Balls, bubbles, planets and scoops of ice-cream are spheres. Let’s learn the two formulas that measure them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Orange peel laid flat covers about four of its middle circles
scenes.breaks: Real peel is thick and tears, so it only roughly shows four circles. 4πr² is exact.
scenes.say: Peel an orange and lay the peel flat. It covers about four circles the same size as the orange’s middle circle. That’s the surface area rule: four pi r squared.

scenes.heading: The sphere formulas
scenes.say: The surface area of a sphere is four pi r squared, and the volume is four thirds pi r cubed. Surface uses r squared, volume uses r cubed. Always use the radius.

scenes.heading: A sphere of radius 9 cm
scenes.say: Here is a sphere, then its radius of nine centimetres. The surface area is four pi times eighty-one, which is three hundred and twenty-four pi, about one thousand and eighteen square centimetres. The volume is four thirds pi times seven hundred and twenty-nine, which is nine hundred and seventy-two pi, about three thousand and fifty-four cubic centimetres.
scenes.caption: A sphere of radius 9 cm. SA = 4π × 81 = 324π ≈ 1017.9 cm². V = ⁴⁄₃π × 729 = 972π ≈ 3053.6 cm³.

scenes.heading: Sphere vs hemisphere
scenes.say: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Its curved surface is two pi r squared, and if it is solid, add the flat circle to get three pi r squared. Its volume is two thirds pi r cubed.

scenes.heading: Composite solid: a silo
scenes.say: This silo is a cylinder of radius four metres and height ten metres, then a hemisphere on top. The cylinder is one hundred and sixty pi. The dome is two thirds of pi times sixty-four. Add them: about six hundred and thirty-six point seven cubic metres.
scenes.caption: A silo: a cylinder (r = 4 m, h = 10 m) with a hemisphere on top. Cylinder 160π + dome ⅔π × 64 ≈ 636.7 m³.

scenes.heading: Working backwards
scenes.question: A sphere has a volume of 36π cm³. Find its radius.
scenes.say: A sphere has volume thirty-six pi. Four thirds pi r cubed equals thirty-six pi. Divide by pi and multiply by three quarters: r cubed is twenty-seven. The cube root of twenty-seven is three, so the radius is three centimetres.
scenes.caption: Volume 36π. ⁴⁄₃πr³ = 36π, so r³ = 36 × ¾ = 27 and r = ∛27 = 3 cm.

scenes.say: Recap. A sphere has surface area four pi r squared and volume four thirds pi r cubed. A solid hemisphere has three pi r squared and two thirds pi r cubed. Halve a diameter first, add the parts of composite solids, and use roots to work backwards. Now try the practice questions!
